# Sun Cured: pack study and journal

*Status: **built; awaiting the owner's review in the gallery.** It studies the previous Camel design, the owner's choice (DECISIONS.md F20).*

*Brand names belong here, in the study, and nowhere that ships.*

## The pack

- **Pack** (research name only): Camel, the filters box.
- **Variant studied:** Filters, **the previous design**: a cream field, brown panels at the top and bottom, the scene inside a vertical oval with a brown ring, and a navy wordmark. It was replaced around 2017 by a white field inside a brick-red frame (notes at the end, for a later variant).
- **References** (links only; nothing is committed):
  - A flat render of the previous box: <https://shop.lowesfoods.com/products/camel-filter-box/63734>
  - An older box ("Turkish & American Blend"), pale cream with a lavender wordmark outlined in navy: <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Camel_filtersbox_rjr.JPG>
  - US Reg. 3,512,391, the previous box: "a camel, pyramid and palm tree design on the front of a cigarette package"; colour not claimed; design codes include "plain single line circles" (the oval): <https://trademark.justia.com/774/33/camel-filters-since-1913-turkish-domestic-77433378.html>
  - Stanford's Camel creative history (SRITA): <https://tobacco-img.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/06212512/camel_creativehistory.pdf>
- **How the research was done** (October 2026, a separate browser session; the full report is [`docs/research/2026-10-first-three-packs.md`](../research/2026-10-first-three-packs.md)). For this design the colours came from a screenshot of a render, which shifts colour, so **every value here is low confidence**. The owner judges them in the gallery.

## What's on it

- **Palette** (low confidence):

  | Colour | Where | Value |
  |---|---|---|
  | Cream | The field | about `#f2e7c9` (not measured; between the ornaments and white) |
  | Pale gold | The corner ornaments | `#d8c28d` |
  | Brown | The bottom panel | `#7b4025` |
  | Rose brown | The top panel | `#8b5544` |
  | Gold | Text on the panels | `#e2c583`–`#eed99b` |
  | Navy | The wordmark | about `#2a335e` |

- **Lettering:**
  - **The wordmark** (high confidence for the description, in every version): wide capitals on an upward arc, calligraphic and uncial-flavoured: a swashed **C** with a curled terminal, a leaning **A** with a flat-cut apex, an **M** with curved flared legs, a round uncial **E**, an **L** whose tail sweeps down and right; flared, wedge-like terminals. Navy here; on the older box, a lavender fill outlined in navy.
  - **Panel text:** "FILTERS" on the top panel; "SINCE 1913 | TURKISH & DOMESTIC BLEND" on the bottom panel; gold on brown. Their exact style wasn't recorded; classical serif capitals fit the family's later type.
- **Shapes:** brown panels across the top and bottom; a vertical oval with a brown ring framing the scene in the middle; arabesque ornaments in the corners of the cream field.
- **The scene:** the camel before pyramids and palms, inside the oval. A registered mark.
- **Material:** printed, matt. Tear strip and foil not found.

## What makes it recognizable

1. **The arched, flared, uncial-like wordmark** in navy on cream.
2. **Cream between brown panels,** top and bottom.
3. **The oval** in the middle of the face.

## Treatment

| Element | Mirror, signal or leave out | How |
|---|---|---|
| Cream | Mirror | The page ground, edge to edge. |
| Brown panels, top and bottom | Mirror | The bar and the masthead's top edge in rose brown, the footer in brown, each with gold text. |
| The uncial wordmark | Mirror the character | The site name in Federant (OFL), navy, in widely spaced capitals: flared, calligraphic capitals. Straight for now: the arc needs a markup change, and the study said to judge the straight version first. Never the wordmark's letters. |
| The oval | Signal | A vertical oval with a brown ring as a medallion holding the post's date and reading time; small ovals as section breaks. Never with anything pictured inside. |
| Gold panel text | Mirror the character | Navigation, labels and the footer in Cinzel (OFL) capitals, gold on brown. |
| Corner ornaments | Signal, plainly | Simple square corner brackets in pale gold around the article. **Not arabesques:** see the watch-out below. |
| The scene | Leave out | A registered mark: no animal, no pyramids, no palms. |

## The page

- **Theme name:** Sun Cured, after the sun-cured oriental tobacco in Turkish blends; tobacco vocabulary, not the brand's (F20).
- **Id:** `sun-cured`.
- **Site name case:** THE SMOKEPIT, in capitals, like the wordmark.
- **Template slots:**
  - **Page ground and masthead band:** cream; a rose-brown band across the top.
  - **Site name and headings:** Federant in navy for the site name; headings in Libre Caslon Text bold, navy.
  - **Secondary type:** Cinzel capitals: gold on brown in the panels, brown on cream elsewhere.
  - **Signature shape:** the oval: the date medallion, and small ovals as section breaks and list bullets.
  - **Material:** none.
  - **Footer and metadata:** the brown bottom panel with gold Cinzel capitals.
  - **The article:** Libre Caslon Text (OFL), a dark brown-black on cream.
- **Tear strip colour:** gold.
- **Literal pack parts:** none.
- **Every surface:**
  - **Home:** posts on the cream, each date in a small oval.
  - **Code blocks:** on a paler cream, framed in a thin brown rule; tokens in navy, brown and a dark gold.
  - **Tables:** brown hairlines, Cinzel headers.
  - **Images:** a thin brown frame.
  - **Links:** brown, underlined (6.6:1 on cream).
  - **Fresh pack:** gold Cinzel capitals on the rose-brown bar.
- **Legibility plan:** article text `#3b2414` on cream (11.8:1); navy on cream 9.8:1; gold on brown 4.8:1 (the lighter gold, 5.8:1). Pale gold never carries text (1.4:1).
- **Endorsement test:** the risk is low: no scene, no wordmark, the oval holds the post's own date, and the name in the flared capitals is the site's own. The real question is the opposite: whether the theme reads as its pack without the scene.
- **Watch-out:** the pack's imagery is a 1913 fantasy of the "exotic" Middle East, and its corner arabesques belong to it. Reaching for arches, arabesques, minaret silhouettes or "oriental" lettering would be a costume and a caricature at once. The theme keeps to the colour, the panels, the oval and the lettering.

## First instincts

- **Drawing pyramids and palms in CSS.** The registered mark, even drawn from scratch. Ruled out.
- **Copying the arabesque corners.** Replaced with plain corner brackets, for the reason above.
- **A grain or paper texture for warmth.** The pack is flat print.
- **Uncial Antiqua for the site name,** because the research said "uncial". In a specimen it's unicase: in capitals, "THE" still reads as "the", which breaks the rule that the site name takes the wordmark's case (F17), and it leans toward a Celtic pub sign. Federant keeps real capitals with the flare.

## What the research corrected

- **The current pack is a different design** (white field, brick-red frame, blue wordmark, since about 2017). The owner chose the previous one, which is what the first draft half-remembered.
- **The wordmark was navy, not brown,** and it's an arched, flared, uncial-flavoured style, which the first draft couldn't describe.
- **The oval was real** in the previous design; it's gone from the current one.

## The current design, for a later variant

White field `#eae8e6` inside a brick-red frame `#97171e` with small inset corners; a blue tab `#003c8f`–`#01479c` breaking the top of the frame; the wordmark in royal blue `#04448e` with a silver-grey offset outline; "FILTERS" in dark red `#8d2221`; the blend line in maroon `#713335`. High confidence, from two manufacturer renders.

## Log

- 2026-10-19: Study written for the owner's review.
- 2026-10-19: Revised with the owner's web research; recommended the current design.
- 2026-10-19: The owner chose the previous design; study rewritten around it. Colours are low confidence for this design.
- 2026-10-19: Built. Federant for the site name, Cinzel 600 for the capitals (navigation, labels, dates, table headers, the footer), Libre Caslon Text for the article and headings; all OFL. The rose-brown panel is the bar, with a gold edge; the brown panel is the footer, full width, gold capitals on brown (5.8:1). The post's date and reading time sit in a vertical oval with a brown ring and a pale-gold inner ring; on the home page each date sits in a small flat oval, and section breaks are small ovals too. Plain pale-gold corner brackets frame the main column. From the first screenshots: the brackets touched the screen edge on a phone, so the column is now inset 8px each side. List bullets stay plain brown discs: an oval that small reads as a dot anyway. All floor tests pass.

## Open questions

- The colours, once seen in the gallery.
- The bar is the only top panel, and it's much thinner than the pack's. A deeper rose-brown band above the site name would be closer; it's held back so the first screen stays the cream.
- The arc on the site name: worth a markup change, after the straight version is judged?
